title: 1979 AHSME Problem 10
statement: If \(P_1P_2P_3P_4P_5P_6\) is a regular hexagon whose apothem (distance from the center to the midpoint of a side) is \(2,\) and \(Q_i\) is the midpoint of side \(P_iP_{i+1}\) for \(i=1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) then the area of quadrilateral \(Q_1Q_2Q_3Q_4\) is

solutions.text:
Let \(O\) be the center. Consecutive apothems \(OQ_i\) and \(OQ_{i+1}\) have length \(2\) and form a \(60^\circ\) angle, so each \(\triangle OQ_iQ_{i+1}\) is equilateral of side \(2.\) The quadrilateral is the union of three such triangles, and hence has area \[ 3\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot2^2\right)=3\sqrt3. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: The points \(Q_i\) lie on a circle of radius equal to the apothem
